messages:
alex: FYI I hit a nasty perf regression in py-sdk async client under 429s. Looks like quota header parsing collapsed multiple buckets into one.

jamie: can you paste the header?

alex: quota-bot logged: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nX-RedQuotas: tokens=150/second; embeddings=10/minute; retry_after=3

sara: our parser only splits on commas, so semicolons break it. we end up using embeddings limit for everything.

jamie: that explains the serialization. under concurrency we starve tokens.

alex: proposal: robust parser that accepts ",", ";" and whitespace; returns map resource -> {limit, window_s, retry_after}. unit tests for header variants.

sara: and client-side: replace global asyncio.Semaphore with per-resource AsyncRateLimiter that has acquire(resource, cost). Also honor retry_after by blocking a resource locally when server says so.

jamie: typing: expose a RateLimiter Protocol so sync/async implementations are swappable; use Literal for resource names.

quota-bot: added sample headers from recent run: X-RedQuotas: tokens=200/second,embeddings=20/minute,retry_after=1

alex: I'll take parser + tests (2d). jamie take async limiter + types (4d). sara will wire into retry middleware + add a debug dump (3d). I'll add a small example under examples/ showing per-resource bursting.

jamie: will open draft PR branch `async/rl-refactor` and tag. quick win: deprecate old parse_quota helper but keep for compat. :thumbsup:
